- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp sentiment spike (≥0.67 with +0.33+ sentiment change), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and news volume remains steady, model overcorrects downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature drop.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (±0.33+ change) and news volume is low; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is below 70.00, model often misses the bottom; apply a “floor” correction: if forecast > 70.00 and sentiment < 0.33, reduce by 1–2%.
- If sentiment change is negative and forecast is rising, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day until sentiment stabilizes.
